subject: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual evals for GlobeBank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@globebank.com>, Luca Rossi <luca.rossi@globebank.eu>
Cc: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:00:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual evals for GlobeBank

Hi Alice / Luca —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the recommended next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of today
- Demo: Redwood inference runtime + routing for production inference; highlighted latency/cost controls.
- Discussed GlobeBank requirements: customer-facing chat across EU & APAC, strict EU data residency for some regions, and high-quality responses in FR/PT-BR/JA.

Model fit recommendations (initial)
- rw7b-chat-q4f: low-latency, strong generalization for short-form responses (good for transactional flows)
- rw13b-chat-q8_0: higher-quality multilingual model; better for nuanced EU languages and longer context
- fallbacks: rw7b-compact for peak traffic to control cost

Requested deliverables (what we’ll do next)
1) Run targeted evals on your sample prompts for FR, PT-BR, JA and share CSV with quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE + human pass/fail) — deliver by Tue 6/23.
2) Share the prompt sets we used and a short guide to avoid quality regressions when changing generation params. Attached: globebank_prompt_set_fr_ja_ptbr_v1.txt
3) Provide a short benchmark report (latency/cost tradeoffs) — will attach globebench_multilingual_results_v1.csv.
4) Follow-up call to review results & mutual action plan — propose Thu 6/24 15:00 UTC (please confirm).

Notes on compliance/residency
- For EU-resident workloads we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with region pinning; we can scope a narrow proof-of-concept if you need an on-prem option for certain datasets.

Next steps for Alice/Luca
- Confirm the languages and any priority locales (e.g., FR-FR vs FR-BE)
- Confirm availability for 6/24 15:00 UTC or propose an alternate slot

I’m looping in Priyom (AE) to help coordinate timelines and Rishi (SE) for the eval work below.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: globebank_prompt_set_fr_ja_ptbr_v1.txt

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@globebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Luca Rossi <luca.rossi@globebank.eu>, procurement@globebank.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:10:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual evals for GlobeBank

Hi Marissa —

Really appreciate the clear recap and recommendations. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Languages/priorities — Primary: French (FR-FR) and Portuguese (PT-BR). Secondary: Japanese (JA). We expect the first two to cover ~70% of non-English traffic across EU and LATAM, but JA is increasingly important for our APAC customers.
2) Residency — For FR and PT-BR user data we need EU residency for processing and logs. For JA we can use APAC region but would prefer dedicated capacity.
3) Evaluation metrics — we’d like both automated metrics and a small human-in-the-loop pass/fail on critical prompt types (account lookup, transaction confirmation, regulatory notices).

6/24 15:00 UTC will work for me; Luca will confirm but he should be available. Please include Rishi for the eval plan.

Also, procurement looped in to start paperwork if we proceed.

Thanks —
Alice Nguyen
Product Lead (AI) — GlobeBank
alice.nguyen@globebank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@globebank.com>, Luca Rossi <luca.rossi@globebank.eu>
Cc: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual evals for GlobeBank

Thanks Alice — great, appreciate the priorities. Looping everyone in with an initial plan and clear owners: 

Action plan (owners & dates)
- Rishi (SE): run targeted evals across FR-FR, PT-BR, JA using the attached prompt set + your internal samples. Deliver CSV + short human-assessment notes by Tue 6/23 EOD.
- Priyom (AE): coordinate procurement docs and confirm PO/contract timeline with procurement@globebank.com.
- Marissa (AE): run model selection & cost/latency tradeoff analysis and share recommended default model profiles for pilot (expected Wed 6/23).

Initial recommended model profiles (for pilot)
- Profile A (latency-optimized): rw7b-chat-q4f pinned in EU region; automatic KV-prefix caching for account lookups.
- Profile B (quality-optimized): rw13b-chat-q8_0 with slightly higher temperature controls and a conservative token budget for regulatory copy.

Quality regression concerns
- We’ll set up a small evaluation harness that records prompts + model outputs so we can reproduce regressions when changing generation params or model weights. We recommend a baseline snapshot before any rollout.

Proposed follow-up call: Thu 6/24 15:00 UTC — please confirm availability.

Marissa

Attachments referenced: globebench_multilingual_results_v1.csv (will populate after Rishi’s run)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@globebank.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual evals for GlobeBank

Thanks Marissa — starting the eval work today. Quick note on scope and what I’ll deliver: 

Eval plan (high level)- Data: will run your provided prompt set + 200 extra prompts for each priority language (FR-FR, PT-BR, JA) covering the three critical flows you mentioned (account lookup, transaction confirmation, regulatory notices).
- Metrics: automated (BLEU, ROUGE, token-length distribution), safety/regulatory keyword checks, and a human pass/fail sample (30 per language).
- Residency/testing: for FR/PT-BR I’ll run inference in our EU dedicated pool to capture realistic latency and to validate residency requirements. For JA I’ll run in APAC dev pool.
- Deliverables: globebench_multilingual_results_v1.csv (CSV with per-prompt metrics), a short write-up with observed failure modes, and a small repro guide for any noted regressions. ETA Tue 6/23 EOD.

Link to initial runner + sample results (internal): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-globebank-eval-drive

I’ll upload the final CSV and ping everyone when ready.

- Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
